title: Customer Clarity Lane and Conditional Commit Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Senior account teams and customer success frequently escalate feature asks and contractual SLAs without clear downstream decisions. This causes ambiguous commitments, rework across engineering/design, and ad-hoc roadmap swaps that harm delivery predictability.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable intake lane (the 'Clarity Lane') for high-touch/top-account escalations that enforces conditional commitments. The lane should produce a deterministic output: either (A) a scoped pledge with a delivery window and tradeoffs, (B) a documented deferral with mitigation plan, or (C) rapid escalation to executive review.

Scope: MVP includes: 1) Intake form in Redwood Console + intake API fields for sales/CS to submit escalations; 2) A scoring rule set to classify requests (urgency, revenue at risk, compliance, engineering effort); 3) Conditional commit templates (Full, Partial, Deferral) and a Triage runbook; 4) Visibility in roadmap planning board and an audit log entry for each decision.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include autoscheduling or budget forecasting; it focuses on intake, scoring, and decision artifacts. Heavy redesign of Console UI will be follow-up (DES backlog).

Deliverables:
- Console intake form + API schema (fields: account_id, request_type, impact_summary, requested_by, target_release_window, must_have_criteria, compliance_flag, supporting_artifacts URL list).
- Scoring engine prototype (serverless rule engine + configurable weights in PM UI).
- Decision templates and triage checklist (PDF/MD) and export to Confluence.
- Pilot rollout to 5 named top accounts for one cycle.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Intake form captures all required fields and writes to the Clarity Lane queue; API schema documented in README.
2) Scoring engine assigns one of three priority buckets (Critical / High / Review) with consistent reproducibility for test cases (see test matrix).
3) For pilot accounts, 80% of submitted escalations result in one of the 3 decision outputs within 7 business days.
4) Roadmap board shows linked decision artifact and auditable change history for any schedule change tied to a Clarity Lane decision.
5) Stakeholders (CS, Sales, Eng, Legal) sign off on templates prior to pilot.

Success metrics (tracked for OKR):
- Reduce untriaged top-account asks older than 30 days from 42% -> <=10% by end of Q2.
- Decrease mid-cycle roadmap ad-hoc scope shifts attributed to escalations by 50% during pilot.
- Achieve >=90% stakeholder satisfaction in pilot feedback survey (N>=8 responses).

Implementation notes:
- Prefer incremental approach: API + basic intake UI -> scoring rules -> templates -> pilot.
- Use existing auth and audit framework from Console (ENG-2101) and Console components from DES-332.
- Storage: decisions persisted in product DB with minimal schema; export endpoint to Confluence for exec summaries.
- Data retention: decision artifacts retained per policy in release; flag for confidential attachments.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: CS may bypass Clarity Lane and use Slack. Mitigation: require intake form link in official escalation playbook and train AE/CS managers; add Slack integration to surface reminders (follow-up ticket).
- Risk: Scoring feels opaque. Mitigation: include transparency modal showing rule weights and example cases.

2026-03-04 - Engineering spike started for scoring prototype (Priya). Chosen approach: rule-based serverless function with config stored in product DB. Eng estimate updated to 3 pts for backend + 2 pts frontend.

2026-03-10 - Pilot candidate list finalized (5 accounts) and CS owners assigned. Rafael circulated pilot playbook for approval. Next milestone: pilot kickoff 2026-04-01.

Review feedback & decisions:
- Decision: Keep initial scoring explainable (no ML) for transparency in pilot.
- Decision: Default retention 2 years for decision artifacts; confidential attachments require KMS encryption (follow-up with Security).

Open questions:
1) Should we auto-create a roadmap ticket when decision = Full commit? (Pro: reduces manual work; Con: might bypass discovery). Proposal: create a stub ticket that requires triage completion before scheduling.
2) Is 7 business days SLA realistic for Compliance-heavy asks? CS suggests 10 days for compliance flagged requests. Proposal: run pilot with 7-day SLA but allow configured extensions per account.
